views.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Use the G20 dinner to lock a time-limited negotiating track whose minimum deliverable is a delay of the January 1, 2019 lift of List 3 from 10% to 25%, and a hold on any remaining-goods list. Keep existing retaliatory tariffs in place as leverage; do not volunteer a new purchase package or structural concessions before the United States puts a matching, written pause on the table. Treat talks as damage control, not a settlement — the May joint statement already showed that an unsecured purchase pledge can be pocketed and then discarded.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Threat is material and rising, but not existential. Combined U.S. Section 301 coverage is already ~$250B, List 3 is scheduled to jump to 25% on 1 Jan 2019, and Washington has teed up ~$267B more if we answer in kind (timeline 2018-09-17/24; contemporaneous USTR and NYT reporting). That sits next to firm-level precedent (ZTE denial order, 2018-04-16) and FX/reserve stress: CNY weakened from ~6.40 in early June to 6.95 by 28 Nov (~8.6%), and reserves fell about $56B over the window to ~$3.08T. Official IP growth slipped to 5.4% YoY and Q3 GDP printed 6.5%, the weakest since 2009. This is the +0.5 CHN band (export exposure, FX pressure, national-champion targeting) minus a notch, because merchandise exports are still roughly holding, reserves remain above $3T, and there is no evidenced financial-stability break. Action should not match the threat with further escalation: another tariff round would likely invite the remaining-goods list and a steeper growth hit (TS Lombard: ~0.5–0.7pp from 2019 if the fight continues), while unilateral purchase/structural concessions would replay May 19–29 (joint statement, then White House proceeds with 301). U.S. politics also create a narrow opening — market drawdown, GM layoffs, and Kudlow/Mnuchin arguing for a pause — so the rational move is negotiate for a tariff freeze, not hold silently and not concede first.
key_factors: G20 Trump-Xi dinner is the only live off-ramp before the 1 Jan 2019 List-3 25% cliff
US already covers ~$250B of Chinese goods and has threatened the remaining ~$267B
CNY ~8.6% weaker since June and FX reserves down to an 18-month-area low; Q3 GDP 6.5%
May 19 purchase-pledge truce collapsed within 10 days — do not pre-commit purchases
ZTE denial order showed non-tariff/tech-chokepoint risk beyond tariffs
Further Chinese escalation would likely be answered with List 4 rather than U.S. de-escalation

sources_cited.excerpt: Trump directs USTR to finalize List 3: 10% tariffs on ~$200B of Chinese imports effective Sept 24, scheduled to rise to 25% on Jan 1, 2019.
List 3 takes effect at 10%. China imposes retaliatory tariffs (5–10%) on ~$60B of US goods. Combined US Section 301 coverage now ~$250B of Chinese imports.
Trump and Xi hold a phone call focused on trade; agree to meet at the G20 in Argentina.
US and China release joint statement after talks: China agrees to "significantly increase" purchases of US goods and services. Mnuchin says trade war is "on hold."
White House announces the US will proceed with Section 301 actions, including 25% tariffs on ~$50B of Chinese imports. Truce collapses.
US Commerce Department bans ZTE from buying US components (denial order). ZTE faces operational shutdown. Major non-tariff escalation.
China reserves ex-gold fell from ~$3.137T (Jul) to ~$3.081T (Nov), about -$56B / -1.8%.
China industrial production YoY index eased from 106.0 (Jul) to 105.4 (Nov).
China merchandise exports still roughly stable (~$206B Jul to $208B Nov, SA), so the real-economy hit is not yet a collapse.

If leaders agree to talks, Trump would most likely postpone the increase to 25% and hold off on ~$267B of new tariffs; Kudlow says a deal is possible but Trump is 'perfectly happy to stand on his tariff policies.'
China Q3 2018 GDP slowed to 6.5% y/y, weakest since Q1 2009, missing expectations.
October reserves fell $33.93B to $3.053T, an 18-month low, as the yuan lost ~10% vs USD since February.
List 3 additional tariffs start at 10% on Sept 24, 2018 and increase to 25% on January 1, 2019.
